subject: Materials Science
title: Thin Film Deposition
description: Learn Thin Film Deposition in one minute.

hook.text: A chip's layers are built one atom at a time — deposited from gas phase onto the silicon surface.

buildup.text: CVD (chemical vapor deposition) flows reactive gases over hot wafers — chemicals react and deposit solid films.

discovery.text: PVD (physical vapor deposition) sputters target atoms onto wafers — ideal for metal interconnect layers.

twist.text: ALD (atomic layer deposition) grows films one atomic layer at a time — perfect conformality on any 3D shape.

climax.text: Gate oxides in modern transistors are only 5 atoms thick — deposited by ALD with atomic precision.

punchline.text: Chips are built by stacking atom-thick films — engineering at nature's limit.

quiz.question: What makes ALD special compared to other deposition methods?
options: It grows exactly one atomic layer per cycle with perfect conformality
It only works on flat surfaces
